thread:
anil: Quick question — about to apply TF for vectorizer svcaccount + KMS key grant in staging. We saw a flake where the sidecar init container error'd because the IRSA annotation hadn't propagated to the pod by the time it started. Posting the plan snippet, any obvious mistakes?

marisa: can you paste the tf plan snippet and the k8s manifest you apply in the same run? usually it's an ordering issue between kubernetes_service_account and the deployment.

anil: sure. plan shows aws_kms_key_policy + aws_kms_grant and kubernetes_service_account with annotation. we create sa via helm chart (helm_release) and also apply the aws iam pieces in same pipeline. snippet:```hcl
resource "aws_kms_grant" "vectorizer_sa" {
  name       = "vectorizer-irsa-grant"
  key_id     = aws_kms_key.vectorizer.id
  grantee_principal = data.aws_iam_role.irsa_role.arn
  operations = ["Decrypt", "GenerateDataKey"]
}

resource "kubernetes_service_account" "vectorizer" {
  metadata {
    name = "vectorizer-sa"
    namespace = "vectorizer-staging"
    annotations = {
      "eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn" = data.aws_iam_role.irsa_role.arn
    }
  }
}
```

jules: a few things: 1) if helm_release creates the SA, TF trying to manage the same SA will race. prefer letting helm own the SA and patch the annotation via a kubernetes_manifest or a helm post-renderer. 2) IRSA relies on projected token + kubelet having the annotation when the pod is created, so ordering must ensure the SA exists with annotation before deployment is scheduled.

sam: also worth noting that KMS grant propagation can take a second or two; the real flake is usually the pod starting before the kube-apiserver sees the SA annotation. In CI we solved similar by adding an explicit dependency (depends_on) from deployment -> kubernetes_service_account resource or by creating a small wait-for-annotation null_resource.

anil: our pipeline currently does: terraform apply (IAM & KMS), then helm upgrade --install (chart creates SA & deployment). So TF created the KMS and role but helm created SA after; that's backwards. I assumed IRSA would work because role exists, but the chart didn't set the annotation until helm ran.

marisa: simplest fix: let TF manage the SA (if you want deterministic ordering) OR modify the helm values to include the annotation (pass the role arn in values) so SA is created annotated on first helm install. If you can't change chart, add a kubernetes_manifest resource after helm that patches the SA and add a depends_on from deployment to that patch.

jules: example kubectl patch we use in a post-hook:```bash
kubectl patch sa vectorizer-sa -n vectorizer-staging --type merge -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn":"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/irsa-vectorizer"}}}'
```

infra-bot: terraform plan check: detected "helm_release.vectorizer" and "kubernetes_service_account.vectorizer" both present. Potential drift: helm owns SA -> TF will try to adopt or error.

sam: alternative: keep helm owning SA, then create a small pre-upgrade hook job (helm hook) that blocks until the SA has the annotation (or adds it). But careful: hooks can complicate rollback.

anil: ok i'm leaning to update chart values to inject annotation on install (we have a wrapper values file). Quick follow-up — for the KMS grant, is granting the role arn (grantee_principal) fine, or should we grant to the OIDC provider/principalTag?

jules: granting to the role ARN is fine for IRSA because the role is what pods assume (sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity). Some shops grant to the OIDC provider + condition on sub to be strict, but role ARN grant is straightforward. For extra safety add a condition on aws:SourceAccount or aws:ViaAWSService depending on your threat model.

marisa: also add a short smoke: deploy a pod with the annotated SA and curl KMS decrypt in it to validate the grant. We do that in a k8s job in staging as a gating step.

anil: thanks all — plan: patch helm values to include eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn, re-run apply, add a small k8s job smoke that fetches a test data key. I'll send the updated values and the smoke job yaml for quick review.

sam: lgtm. if you still hit races, we can add a null_resource local-exec with a kubectl wait --for=condition=... on the SA to ensure annotation exists before deployment.

anil: noted. will follow up in a PR. :thumbsup:
